author: Codex documentation author; corrections by DOC-029 source-review author agent (documents)

prerequisites: Signed-in fictional role in its own browser context on the work documentation lab; a second session of the same role for the stale-state check.

Walkthrough-created Contracts with a three-Version Primary Document pinned on v2 and further disposable Documents, and Knowledge Items with two Documents, all named with DOC-029 documents and a run stamp.
Record archive and restore, the second session's restore, and the rename during the delete dialog were API fixture actions.
scenarios.expected: Archive/restore preserves supported history; permanent deletion removes the documented Versions/files and references. Other roles cannot perform Administrator deletion; consequences and unavailable-file behavior match the guide.
scenarios.actual: 7 recorded browser steps passed for this role. Archive from the Actions menu removed the Document; Show archived showed its Archived row, and the read-back kept three Versions, Primary, the Executed pin on v2 and downloadable files. Restore from the row menu brought it back with its designations. Checkboxes with Archive and then Restore in the selection bar archived and restored two Documents. While the Contract was archived there was no Show archived or Upload, only Compare in row menus, and restore was refused with 409 until the Contract was restored. After another session restored a Document, Restore on the stale row showed "This document is not archived." and a reload showed it live. This role had no Delete in the row menu or selection bar and a direct deletion answered 403 with all three Versions kept. A Knowledge Item's Documents section archived and restored a Document, offered Set as primary and had no New folder.

prerequisites: Signed-in fictional role in its own browser context on the work documentation lab; a second session of the same role for the stale-state check.

Walkthrough-created Contracts with a three-Version Primary Document pinned on v2 and further disposable Documents, and Knowledge Items with two Documents, all named with DOC-029 documents and a run stamp.
Record archive and restore, the second session's restore, and the rename during the delete dialog were API fixture actions.
scenarios.expected: Archive/restore preserves supported history; permanent deletion removes the documented Versions/files and references. Other roles cannot perform Administrator deletion; consequences and unavailable-file behavior match the guide.
scenarios.actual: 11 recorded browser steps passed for this role. Archive from the Actions menu removed the Document; Show archived showed its Archived row, and the read-back kept three Versions, Primary, the Executed pin on v2 and downloadable files. Restore from the row menu brought it back with its designations. Checkboxes with Archive and then Restore in the selection bar archived and restored two Documents. While the Contract was archived there was no Show archived or Upload, only Compare in row menus, and restore was refused with 409 until the Contract was restored. After another session restored a Document, Restore on the stale row showed "This document is not archived." and a reload showed it live. Delete opened "Delete this document?" naming the Document and its 3 versions; Delete stayed disabled until delete was typed and Cancel kept the Document. A rename while the dialog was open made the deletion refused. Typing delete removed the Document, its three Version downloads answered 404, no other Document became Primary, and the Contract activity still named it. Selection-bar Delete of two Documents also needed delete typed. An earlier Version's menu had no Delete and a single-Version delete answered 404. A Knowledge Item's Documents section archived and restored a Document, offered Set as primary and had no New folder.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the article author and the source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

Removal of stored originals, previews and extracted text was observed through 404 Version downloads, not by listing the storage volume. Audit log entries were not read; the Contract activity read was.
A storage failure during deletion was not produced, so the partial-failure paragraph was not exercised.

When a rename made the deletion refuse, the dialog's message read "Type the document's name exactly to delete it." while the dialog asks for the word delete. The refusal matches the article; the message wording is reported separately as a possible product issue.
Removal from normal search after archive was not checked.
Business User limits (no archive, restore or delete controls, 403 for each) are a supplementary business_user step; V-C54 does not require that role.
